texts.preamble: Ram Ratan Agarwal vs The State Of Jharkhand on 18 April, 2023 Author: Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi Bench: Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi Cr .M.P. No. 2023 of 2011 Ram Ratan Agarwal ..... ... Petitioner Versus 1. The State of Jharkhand. 2. Sri Krishna Prasad Singh ..... ... Opposite Parties -------- Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi ------ For the Petitioner : Mr. Shankar Lal Agrawal, Advocate. For the State : Mr. Bishambhar Shastri, A.P.P. ------ 10/ 18.04.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties. 2. This petition has been filed for quashing of the entire complaint including the order taking cognizance dated 22.09.2009, by which, cognizance for the offences under Section 16(1)(a)(i)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has been taken against the petitioner, in connection with C-IV/13/09 (T.R. No. 1407/09), pending in the court of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi.
texts.facts: 2. This petition has been filed for quashing of the entire complaint including the order taking cognizance dated 22.09.2009, by which, cognizance for the offences under Section 16(1)(a)(i)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has been taken against the petitioner, in connection with C-IV/13/09 (T.R. No. 1407/09), pending in the court of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi. 3. Complaint case was filed alleging therein that the samples of alleged adulterated Cadbury Chocolate have been collected from the premises of one Ram Ratan Agarwal on 03.06.2009. It is further alleged that on analysis, the Public Analyst, Ranchi vide his report No. 544, dated 27.06.2009, enclosed with prosecution report, has opined that the filled chocolate (Cadbury 5 Star) does not confirm the standard of quality as laid down under the P.F.A. Rules, 1955 and as such, it was found to be adulterated by virtue of presence of hydrogenated vegetable fat. 4.
texts.arguments: Mr. Agrawal, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the O.P. No. 2 has filed a complaint petition alleging therein that Cadbury Five Star chocolate was found adulterated is wholly without jurisdiction in the teeth of definition of 'filled chocolate' given in Appendix-B of A.25.03. He further submits that Appendix-B has been issued under Rule-5 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955. Rule-5 states that standard of quality of various articles specified in Appendix-B to the rules is defined in that appendix. Appendix A.25.03 states about the standard of chocolate. He further submits that the chocolate shall not contain any vegetable fat other than cocoa butter. He further submits that in the Prevention of Food Adulteration Ac, 1954, the chocolate has also been defined.. He further submits that the case of the main accused namely Pawan Kumar Agarwal @ Pawan Agarwal has already been [LEAKAGE_MASK] by this court in Cr.M.P. No. 196 of 2011 by order dated 01.09.2011 [reported in 2012 (2) JCR 395 Jhr]. On these grounds, he submits that entire criminal proceedings are bad in law and the same may kindly be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 5. On the other hand, Mr. Shastri, learned A.P.P. appearing for the State submits that as per the norms prescribed in the Rule for manufacturing of filled chocolate, it is necessary for the manufacturer to coat 25% chocolate over the filled item. Thus, the said chocolate content require to fulfill the norms prescribed for chocolate. He submits that the norms prescribed for the chocolate clearly show that no hydrogenated vegetable fact can be used for its manufacturing. On these grounds, he submits that the learned court has rightly taken the cognizance and no interference is required by this court.
